analysis:
Examined the diagnostic-only CLI changes. DoctorRunner.swift head 37-38, DoctorCommand.swift head 358-363 and StatusCommand.swift head 148-153 now read `displayedProviderAuthorization` (shown authorization) separately from `currentProviderAuthorization` (passed as removalAuthorization into ProviderAuthorizationReadiness.summary). Both values come from the local daemon state file and only affect operator-facing text and doctor pass/warn/exit levels. Neither alters provider serving, admission, coordinator authorization, attestation or key custody (TB-011, T-052, T-053, T-057, TB-009, TB-003).

The doctor/status trust classification (`appAttestAuthorized`, DoctorRunner head 39; DoctorCommand head 363) is now derived from the displayed authorization rather than the current one. This could change which hints are suppressed (MDM enrollment, attestation readiness) or produce a misleading `.pass`. That would be a diagnostic accuracy issue, not a security control, since the coordinator remains authoritative for serving permission (T-052).

The definitions of `displayedProviderAuthorization` and the new `summary(removalAuthorization:)` overload are outside the supplied source. Integration should confirm three points:
- `displayedProviderAuthorization` stays coordinator-URL bound like `currentProviderAuthorization`.
- `hasCurrentAppAttestAuthorization(now:)` still enforces expiry on the displayed record, so a lapsed or revoked grant is not shown as a current pass (T-053/T-057 operator-misstatement risk; cf. T-058 "misstate trust").
- The Machine ID printed in StatusCommand comes from the displayed record. It is a local identifier shown to the owner, which is not a new exposure.

No network, file-write or privilege changes were introduced. No regression was identified from the visible evidence.
